      How it works, and what it can't see

      • Model: Excel's Regression tool (ordinary least squares) with Y = sale price ÷ square feet and 16 X columns, Excel's limit: square feet, bedrooms, bathrooms, co-op, doorman, outdoor space, and 10 of 11 regions. The left-out region is the baseline the others are compared with.
      • Why price per square foot: a regression on price itself missed by about 28% on sales it hadn't seen and predicted negative prices for 36 small apartments. Price per square foot misses by about 20% and never goes negative, and it's how Manhattan prices are quoted.
      • Accuracy: each sale was priced by a model fitted without it (5-fold cross-validation). The ranges come from those misses.
      • Can't see: floor and view from the unit, light, renovation, building age and fees (common charges, maintenance), co-op board rules, and when each sale happened (the file has no dates).
      • Region, not block: location enters only through 11 broad regions, so two apartments in the same region but on very different blocks get the same location value.

      Sources

      • Sales: StreetEasy sale records compiled by the project team. Only the fitted model is on this page, no sale records.
      • Map: OpenStreetMap contributors.
      • Building lookup: NYC Department of City Planning, PLUTO (public record).
